items.imageObservation: The image is a mind map titled '10 Building Blocks of an Agentic AI System'. It visually connects a central 'AI' icon to ten distinct blocks: Foundation Model, Agent Orchestration, Context & Instructions, Memory & State, Knowledge & RAG, Tools & Actions, Planning & Workflow, Multi-Agent Collaboration, Security & Guardrails, and Observability & Evaluation. Each block has a brief description of its function and lists example tools. The author's name, Shalini Goyal, is also present in the center.
items.text: An LLM is not an AI agent. It becomes agentic when the system around it can understand goals, plan work, use tools, remember context, act, and recover from failure. Here are the 10 building blocks: → Foundation Model Provides reasoning, generation, understanding, and tool calling. → Agent Orchestration Routes tasks, manages workflows, maintains state, and handles retries. → Context and Instructions Defines goals, rules, requirements, task context, and tools. → Memory and State Retains conversation history, preferences, progress, and knowledge. → Knowledge and RAG Retrieves trusted information and grounds responses. → Tools and Actions Calls APIs, queries databases, executes code, and triggers actions. → Planning and Workflow Breaks complex goals into tasks, sequences them, and tracks progress. → Multi-Agent Collaboration Lets specialized agents delegate, hand off, and coordinate work. → Security and Guardrails Controls identity, permissions, tool access, filtering, and approval. → Observability and Evaluation Tracks quality, cost, tool calls, failures, and performance. A strong model can produce a good answer. A strong agentic system can complete useful work safely and repeatedly. The advantage will not come from choosing one model. It will come from designing the system around it. Which building block is your team prioritizing? BTW, pre-order for the book is now open! Get your copy of System Design and Behavioral Intelligence here: Amazon: https://lnkd.in/gBEqJpHd

items.evidenceQuote: The goal is not to put AI everywhere. It is to place the right level of automation inside the right process, with the right controls and human oversight.
items.imageObservation: The image is a two-part decision tree. Part 1, 'Should AI Handle This Process At All?', guides the user through questions about process characteristics (repetitive, structured inputs, data type, sensitivity, risk, empathy) to determine if automation, GenAI, human-led AI, or manual processing is appropriate. Part 2, 'Which Enterprise AI Tool Fits?', then directs the user based on process type (internal, customer-facing, legacy apps, data sync, custom models, analytics) to specific platforms like ServiceNow, UiPath, Salesforce, Azure OpenAI, or Power BI.
items.text: AI should not handle everything. The enterprise AI decision is knowing what to automate, what to augment, and what should remain human. Before selecting a tool, start with the process: → Is it repetitive and high-volume? → Are the inputs structured and rules clear? → Is the work based on text, documents, or emails? → Does it involve sensitive data? → Does it require judgment or empathy? → Could a mistake create legal, financial, or safety risks? → Would automation save enough time? Clear rules and structured inputs may be ready for automation. Unstructured work may need GenAI. Sensitive workflows require guardrails. High-risk decisions should stay human-led, while AI assists with drafting. Only then should you choose the platform. → ServiceNow for tickets, approvals, employee workflows, and knowledge. → UiPath or Automation Anywhere for legacy applications. → Power Automate, Zapier, or n8n for simple team workflows. → Salesforce Agentforce or Zendesk AI for customer-facing processes. → Integration Hub for synchronizing data across systems. → Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, or Vertex AI for custom applications. → Power BI or Tableau for analytics and dashboards. The goal is not to put AI everywhere. It is to place the right level of automation inside the right process, with the right controls and human oversight. What process inside your enterprise would you evaluate first?

items.evidenceQuote: An enterprise needs a trusted harness around all of its AI.
items.text: Every enterprise now has access to intelligence — models keep getting smarter, agents keep multiplying, and AI is showing up everywhere you look. But intelligence alone was never the hard part. The hard part is trust: can AI actually understand your business, and can it act on it safely, inside your governance, your security, your rules? Most AI harnesses out there wrap around a single agent. That's not enough. An enterprise needs a trusted harness around all of its AI. This week we introduced the Salesforce Trusted Enterprise AI Harness. It's built on six capabilities, working as one system: 🧠Trusted Context — customer data, metadata, semantics, knowledge, real-time signals, and memory 🤖Trusted Agency — reasoning, planning, memory, and orchestration, balanced with deterministic controls ⚡Trusted Action — secure connections to apps, APIs, workflows, and business processes 📋Trusted Governance — lineage, quality, guardrails, and controls over data, metadata, and policies 🔒Trusted Security — identity, permissions, data protection, privacy, and runtime security ⚙️Trusted Models — intelligent routing to the right model based on accuracy, performance, cost, and business need This is decades of Salesforce innovation — Data 360, Informatica, MuleSoft and Agent Fabric, Tableau, Agentforce, Salesforce Guardian and the Salesforce Platform — coming together into one open architecture. And it goes wherever you go. Our harness extends into whatever AI experience customers choose — Claude, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Agentforce, and beyond. Wherever the AI experience lives, the Salesforce Trusted Enterprise AI Harness can bring the enterprise with it. The agent harness makes an agent work. The Trusted Enterprise AI Harness makes AI work for the enterprise. That is the future we are building at Salesforce. See it in action at Dreamforce. 🚀 https://lnkd.in/drfmV3Be

items.evidenceQuote: The advantage comes from connecting every layer. Strategy gives AI a purpose. Architecture makes it usable. Governance makes it trustworthy. Platforms make it scalable. That is the difference between an impressive AI demo and a capability people can rely on every day.
items.imageObservation: The image is a mind map titled 'Enterprise AI Quick Guide' with four main branches: AI Strategy & Readiness, Enterprise AI Governance & Controls, Core Enterprise AI Architecture, and Enterprise AI Platforms & Tools. Each branch has sub-nodes detailing specific aspects like 'Model Risk Management' under Governance, 'RAG' under Architecture, and various platform examples. The visual reinforces the interconnectedness of these components.
items.text: A powerful model is only the beginning. Enterprise AI creates value when strategy, data, architecture, governance, and execution work as one system. Buying an LLM will not create that system. An enterprise AI foundation needs four connected layers: → Strategy and Readiness Start with a business problem. Confirm the data is usable, secure ownership, prioritize use cases, define ROI, and decide where to build or buy. → Core AI Architecture Connect trusted data. Use RAG for grounded responses, agents for multi-step workflows, and human review for sensitive decisions. Add memory, orchestration, APIs, evaluation, and observability. → Governance and Controls Define who can access what. Protect sensitive data, apply guardrails, test security, maintain audit trails, monitor model behavior, and manage the AI lifecycle. → Platforms and Tools Microsoft Foundry, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, Databricks, Snowflake, ServiceNow, and agent frameworks can speed up delivery. But tools cannot replace a clear operating model. The advantage comes from connecting every layer. Strategy gives AI a purpose. Architecture makes it usable. Governance makes it trustworthy. Platforms make it scalable. That is the difference between an impressive AI demo and a capability people can rely on every day. Where is your organization strongest today: strategy, architecture, governance, or execution?
items.topicSummary: The post outlines four interconnected layers for enterprise AI: Strategy, Architecture, Governance, and Platforms. It emphasizes that a clear operating model, not just tools, is crucial for successful AI implementation.
items.whySelected: The post explicitly asks about the operating model and its importance, which aligns with Balasubramaniam's expertise in process redesign and governance. The comment focuses on a practical implication of the operating model within the governance layer, avoiding generic advice.
